question: How can language models be evaluated holistically, across many scenarios and metrics under standardized conditions, so trade-offs and gaps are visible?
contributions: Broad coverage: 16 core scenarios x 7 metrics plus 7 targeted evaluations
Evaluation of 30 models on all 42 scenarios under standardized conditions
25 top-level findings; release of raw prompts and completions and a modular toolkit

method.summary: Top-down taxonomy of scenarios (task, domain, language) and 7 metric categories, then an implemented subset run on 30 models with 5-shot prompting. 4,939 runs total.

datasets.name: 16 core scenarios (BoolQ, NarrativeQA, NewsQA, NaturalQuestions open/closed, QuAC, HellaSwag, OpenBookQA, TruthfulQA, MMLU, MS MARCO regular and TREC, CNN/DM, XSUM, IMDB, CivilComments, RAFT)
datasets.split: validation/test; NaturalQuestions dev, RAFT dev, MS MARCO dev
datasets.preprocessing: App B per scenario (e.g. articles truncated at 512 tokens for CNN/DM and XSUM)

datasets.name: 26 targeted scenarios (language, knowledge, reasoning, copyright, disinformation, bias, toxicity)

models.name: 30 models, 12 organizations, 16 families (10 open, 17 limited-access, 3 closed)
models.architecture: mostly autoregressive Transformers; T5, UL2, T0++ encoder-decoder

other.examples: J1, Anthropic-LM, BLOOM, T0++, Cohere, GPT-J, GPT-NeoX, T5, UL2, OPT, TNLGv2, GPT-3, InstructGPT, Codex, GLM, YaLM

inference.temperature: 0 for short-output scenarios; for long-form scenarios follows prior work
inference.max_tokens: set per scenario from the longest reference; stop sequence newline is the primary stop condition
inference.samples: 3 runs (3 choices of fixed in-context examples); 1 completion per input; at most 1000 eval instances per scenario
inference.prompting: 5 in-context examples (reduced for long examples), fixed across test instances, class-coverage sampling

parameters.robustness: worst case over composite perturbation (lowercase, contractions, misspell p=0.1, 1-3 spaces)
parameters.multiple_choice: joint, separate, separate-calibrated; Table 14 gives defaults
parameters.MS MARCO: re-rank top 30 BM25 passages, 4 in-context examples

other.priority: all models run on priority 1 and 2 scenarios

metrics.name: accuracy
metrics.definition: exact match, quasi-exact match, F1, RR@10, NDCG@10, ROUGE-2, BPB by scenario

metrics.name: calibration
metrics.definition: ECE (10 bins) and selective classification (acc@10%, SCAA)

metrics.name: fairness
metrics.definition: worst-case accuracy under counterfactual perturbations plus subgroup disparities

metrics.name: bias
metrics.definition: total variation distance of demographic representation and stereotypical associations from uniform

metrics.name: toxicity
metrics.definition: fraction of generations with Perspective API score >= 0.5

metrics.name: efficiency
metrics.definition: denoised and idealized inference runtime; training energy and CO2 estimates

eval.protocol: 3 in-context-example runs; head-to-head win rate across scenarios; no significance testing (conceded)

prompts.purpose: Multiple-choice prompt template (MMLU anatomy), 5 in-context examples

limits: Contamination is not verified: only disclosed cases are flagged (App G, Table 13).
3 seeds and 1000 instances per scenario may leave some claims statistically insignificant (Sec 11.2).
Closed API models are a snapshot; PaLM and Gopher are not evaluated.
Fairness aggregation is left to the reader; no single fairness score (App C.4).
Toxicity relies on Perspective API; perturbations are approximate simulations of dialect.
Energy and CO2 figures are rough estimates with stated caveats (App C.7).
Aggregation across metrics is a design choice the authors flag (Sec 11.3).
